heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 can push Polymaker PolyLite ABS up to 214 mm/s under its 18 mm³/s volumetric flow ceiling, but its open-frame design makes parts highly prone to warping and layer separation. Reliable printing demands an ambient draft shield or DIY enclosure along with maxing out the bed temperature at 98°C.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with Magigoo or PVP Glue Stick release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap Maximum Volumetric Speed at 18 mm³/s in filament settings to prevent underextrusion at high speeds.
Set Bed Temperature to 98°C and Nozzle Temperature to 255°C to maximize layer bonding on the open bed.
Enable a 5mm to 8mm Outer Brim with a 0.0mm Brim-Object Gap to anchor sharp corners against warping.
Disable the auxiliary cooling fan entirely and set layer cooling fan to 0% normal, scaling to 15% only for overhangs.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe corner lifting and bed detaching
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: High thermal shrinkage of ABS exposed to open-air convection currents and drafts.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Clean bed with isopropyl alcohol, apply PVP glue stick, set bed temp to 98°C, and use a 10mm brim with a draft shield.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Rapid differential cooling between layers due to unheated ambient air and excessive fan speed.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Turn part cooling fan down to 0%, increase nozzle temp to 260°C, and place an external enclosure over the A1.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Stringing, whisker artifacts, and nozzle popping
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PolyLite ABS has absorbed atmospheric moisture during storage or open-air use.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool in a dedicated dryer at 70°C for at least 6 hours before printing.

faq.question: Can I print large ABS parts on an open-frame Bambu Lab A1?
faq.answer: Large parts will struggle due to ABS thermal contraction in an open room; small components print fine, but large prints require an enclosure.

faq.question: Does Polymaker PolyLite ABS require a hardened steel nozzle on the A1?
faq.answer: No, standard PolyLite ABS is non-abrasive, meaning the stock stainless steel nozzle handles it without premature bore wear.

faq.question: Is it safe to run the Bambu Lab A1 bed at 98°C continuously?
faq.answer: Yes, the A1 bed is rated up to 100°C, making 98°C within its safe operating limits for ABS adhesion.

faq.question: Do I need to manage fumes when printing PolyLite ABS on the A1?
faq.answer: Yes, ABS emits styrene and VOCs during printing; operate the printer in a well-ventilated room or with an active carbon air filter.
